title: Security Awareness and Measuring Cybersecurity Effectiveness

header.html: 2.3 Understand security awareness: Organizational culture (for example importance of security, security leadership); Concepts (for example social engineering, password protection, phishing). 2.4 Measure cybersecurity effectiveness: Key metrics, Key Risk Indicators (KRI); Dashboards, score cards, reports
the official ISC2 CC exam outline

html:
1Awareness, training and education

People are both the weakest link and the best sensor. A good program builds habits.

Level Audience and aim Example
Awareness Everyone; recognize a risk and report it A short yearly course, posters, phishing tips
Training A role; build skills to do a task securely Secure coding for developers
Education Career depth; deep knowledge A degree or advanced course

2Organizational culture and leadership

A security culture means that security is part of how people work.

Element Fact
Tone from the top Leaders follow the rules themselves and fund security
Security leadership A named leader, such as a chief information security officer (CISO), sets direction
No-blame reporting People report mistakes and suspicious messages without fear
Security champions Volunteers in each team who spread good practice
Exam tip

. Culture starts with leaders. If staff fear punishment for reporting a click on a phishing link, incidents stay hidden.

3Social engineering and phishing

Social engineering tricks people into giving access or information. It attacks the human, not the software.

Attack How it works
Phishing Fake email that asks for data or a click, sent to many people
Spear phishing Targeted at one person or group, using personal details
Whaling Spear phishing aimed at executives
Vishing Voice call (phone)
Smishing Text message (SMS)
Pretexting An invented story to gain trust and information
Baiting A tempting item, such as an infected USB drive left lying around
Tailgating (piggybacking) Following an authorized person through a secured door
Shoulder surfing, dumpster diving Watching a screen; searching trash for secrets

Red flags: urgency, unexpected request, mismatched sender or link, pressure to bypass the process, requests for credentials or payment. Report it; do not click.

AI raises the stakes: attackers use AI to write convincing phishing, clone voices and make deepfake video calls, so verify through a second channel.

4Password protection

Good habit Why
Long, unique passwords (a passphrase) Length beats complexity; reuse spreads a breach
Password manager Lets you use a different strong password everywhere
Multi-factor authentication A stolen password alone is not enough
Never share or write passwords in plain sight Accounts must be traceable to one person
Exam tip

. Phishing is many, spear phishing is one, whaling is the executive. Tailgating is physical; phishing is email.

5Measuring effectiveness

You cannot manage what you do not measure. Metrics show whether controls work.

Term Meaning Example
Metric A measurement Number of phishing emails reported
Key performance indicator (KPI) Shows how well you meet a goal Patch compliance of 95 percent against a target of 98
Key risk indicator (KRI) An early warning that risk is rising Growing count of overdue critical patches; spike in failed logins

Typical security metrics: phishing simulation click rate and report rate, mean time to detect (MTTD), mean time to respond (MTTR), number of incidents, open vulnerabilities by age, training completion. AI-specific KRIs include model drift and AI-assisted attack attempts.

Format Purpose
Dashboard Live or frequent view of key numbers, for operations
Scorecard Compares results with targets over time, for managers
Report Detailed, periodic write-up for leaders and auditors
Exam tip

. KPI looks back at performance; KRI looks ahead at danger. Pick the dashboard for live view, the report for detail.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1An email addressed to the chief financial officer by name refers to a real project and asks for an urgent wire transfer. What attack is this?

  • ASmishing, a phishing attack sent by SMS text message
  • BBaiting, a trap that uses a tempting item
  • CWhaling, a targeted phishing attack on an executive
  • DTailgating, an entry into a secure building
Show the answer

Answer: C. A targeted phishing attack aimed at a senior executive is whaling.

S2A caller claims to be from the help desk and asks an employee to read out a six-digit code. Which attack is this?

  • ASmishing, because it uses a text message
  • BDumpster diving, because it needs trash
  • CVishing, because it uses a voice call
  • DShoulder surfing, because it watches a screen
Show the answer

Answer: C. A phone call that tries to trick the victim is vishing.

S3An unknown person walks into a secured office behind an employee who holds the door. What is this called?

  • ATailgating, following into a secured area
  • BPhishing, a fraudulent email attack
  • CPretexting, an invented story attack
  • DWhaling, targeting a senior executive by email
Show the answer

Answer: A. Following an authorized person through a secured door is tailgating.

S4Which measure is a key risk indicator rather than a performance indicator?

  • APatch compliance reached 98 percent last month
  • BA rising number of overdue critical patches
  • CTraining completion reached 100 percent
  • DThe yearly audit passed without findings
Show the answer

Answer: B. A KRI is an early warning that risk is rising, such as growing overdue critical patches.

S5A security manager wants a quick, live view of alerts and open incidents for the operations team. Which format fits best?

  • AAn annual report with detailed findings
  • BA scorecard compared with yearly targets
  • CA dashboard with current key numbers
  • DA policy document with approvals
Show the answer

Answer: C. A dashboard gives a live or frequent view of key numbers for operations.

S6Staff receive a video call that looks like the chief executive and asks for a payment. What is the best response?

  • AVerify the request through a second, known channel
  • BPay at once because the person is visible
  • CReply by email and ask for the amount
  • DIgnore the call and say nothing to anyone
Show the answer

Answer: A. AI can fake voices and video, so verify through a separate known channel and report it.

6.2 Recall questions

R1What is phishing sent to one person called?

Show the answer

Spear phishing.

R2What does SMS-based phishing have as a name?

Show the answer

Smishing.

R3What is the difference between a KPI and a KRI?

Show the answer

A KPI shows performance against a goal; a KRI warns that risk is rising.

R4Who is the audience of awareness training?

Show the answer

Everyone in the organization.

R5What does tone from the top mean?

Show the answer

Leaders follow and fund the security rules themselves.

R6What does a password manager enable?

Show the answer

A different strong password for every account.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Levels awareness (all), training (role), education (depth)
Culture tone from the top, CISO, no-blame reporting, champions
Attacks phishing, spear, whaling, vishing, smishing, pretexting, baiting, tailgating
AI convincing phishing, voice cloning, deepfakes; verify by a second channel
Measures KPI (performance), KRI (early warning), MTTD, MTTR
Formats dashboard (live), scorecard (targets), report (detail)
